To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

puromycin, cis-hydroxy proline, and hydroxynorevaline inhibit collagen synthesis and that the inhibition of synthesis is more than can be explained by the increase in intracellular degradation that these agents cause.

puromycin, a threonin analog, and cis-hyroxproline, an amino acid analog, cause increases in intracellular collagen degradation that are similar to those seen in cells exposed to cycloheaximide and that the increases in degradation are not sufficient to account for the decreases in net production of collagen.
puromycin and cis-hydroxproline cause a reduction in collagen synthesis, and that this reduction is not due to an increased rate of degradation of procollagen molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects on collagen synthesis, intracellular degradation, and secretion in human fibroblasts of agents that cause various defects in collagen.
the effects of agents which cause different kinds of defects in the synthesis of procollagen.
the mechanisms that determine the rate of collagen synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

puromycin, cis-hydroxy-proline and hydroxyno-valine inhibit collagen production by interfering with the synthesis of procollagen molecules, and that the degradation of these abnormal procollagen molecules is increased.

the effects of puromycin, cis-hydroxy-proline, and hydroxynorevaline on collagen synthesis and intracellular degradation were qualitatively similar to those of cycloheximidine but quantitatively less pronounced.
the effects of these agents on collagen synthesis are complex and that the net result is a significant decrease in collagen production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
agents that cause different types of defects in collagen synthesis all inhibit collagen production and increase intracellular degradation of procollagen molecules.

agents that interfere with procollagen folding or with pro-alpha chain assembly, and agents that cause premature release of nasent polypeptides, increase the intracellular degradation of procollagen molecules, but that the increases in degradation cannot account completely for the decrease in collagen production.
agents that cause a variety of defects in procollagen synthesis and folding result in increased intracellular degradation, which is not the sole mechanism by which collagen production is inhibited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of agents on collagen production cannot be understood without considering their effects on both synthesis and degradation.
the degradation of newly synthesized procollagens and pro-alpha chains is not simply a consequence of their abnormal structure.

the degradation of collagen in the cell culture system we employed is not simply the consequence of a defect in the collagen molecule, but rather is the result of the combined effects of a defect in collagen and the inhibition of collagen synthesis.
